questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution deals with the parliament and it's proceedings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 79 to 122**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 79 to 122** of the Indian Constitution deals with the Parliament of India and its proceedings.
 
• These articles cover various aspects such as the composition of Parliament, the powers, and functions of its members, and the procedures for conducting parliamentary business.
 
• Article 79 establishes a bicameral legislature at the federal level, consisting of the President and two Houses: the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• Articles 85 to 122 provide detailed provisions regarding the functioning of Parliament, including sessions, prorogation, dissolution, the conduct of business, and the powers and privileges of its members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 51A**

 
 
• Article 51A specifies the fundamental duties of every citizen of India.
 
• It was added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• These duties include respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property, among others.
 
 
 
• **Article 36 to 51**
 
 
• These articles pertain to the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• They provide guidelines to the central and state governments for making policies aimed at establishing a just society.
 
 
 
• **Article 12 to 35**
 
 
• These articles cover the Fundamental Rights guaranteed to the citizens of India.
 
• They include rights like the right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.

questions.question: A Money Bill should be returned to the Lok Sabha within ______ days by Rajya Sabha, either with recommendations or without recommendations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **As per Article 109 of the Indian Constitution**, if a **Money Bill **is passed by Lok Sabha and transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations, Rajya Sabha must return the Bill to Lok Sabha within 14 days from the date of receipt of the Bill.
 
• If Rajya Sabha fails to return the Bill within this period, the Bill is deemed to have been passed by both the Houses.
 
• If Rajya Sabha wants to make any recommendations to the Money Bill, it can do so within the 14-day period.
 
• Such recommendations may either be accepted or rejected by Lok Sabha. However, if Rajya Sabha fails to return the Bill within 14 days and the Bill is deemed to have been passed, it cannot make any recommendations to the Bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A Money Bill is a type of financial legislation that can only be introduced in Lok Sabha and not in Rajya Sabha. It deals with matters such as taxation, borrowing of money by the government, expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, etc.
 
• Unlike ordinary bills, Money Bills do not require the approval of Rajya Sabha. However, Rajya Sabha can make recommendations to the Bill, which Lok Sabha can either accept or reject.
 
• If there is a disagreement between the two Houses regarding a Money Bill, it is resolved by a joint sitting of both the Houses, where the Bill is passed by a simple majority of the total number of members of both the Houses.
 
• The Speaker of Lok Sabha is the final authority on the question of whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not. If there is any dispute regarding this, the Speaker's decision is final.

• The first general election set the stage for the practice of regular, free, and fair elections in India, reinforcing democratic values.
 
• The successful conduct of the election was a testament to the administrative capabilities of the newly independent nation.
 
• The first Lok Sabha had a tenure from **1952 to 1957**, with Dr. Rajendra Prasad serving as the President of India and Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru as the Prime Minister.

• **Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The Deputy Speaker assists the Speaker in their duties and presides over the Lok Sabha in the Speaker's absence.
 
• The Deputy Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha from amongst themselves.

• The Speaker nominates a panel of not more than ten members to preside over the House in the absence of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
